grid: All four fine-tuned settings score **30.2–36.8%** on the selection rule, **below the frozen-encoder text MLP (39.5%)** and text LR (39.2%). The selected setting is **lr 1e-5 with all layers trained (36.8%)**, but the top three are within 0.3 points, which is pure noise. The four settings used **72.5 min** of GPU time; with seed 1 (22.2 min) the total is about **95 min**, close to the 1.5 h budget.
overfit: **Yes, there is overfitting, and it grows with learning rate and training-set size.** The clearest case is **lr 2e-5 with all layers on WF 2024-H1**: the stopping-set loss is lowest after epoch 1 (1.19), then rises to 1.53 by epoch 3 while the training loss falls from 1.23 to 0.42. Mild overfitting (stopping-set loss up 0.003–0.015 after epoch 2) appears on val for three of four settings. **Freezing the lower half helps but does not remove it**: at lr 2e-5 the stopping-set loss on WF 2024-H1 rises only 0.003 instead of 0.33. Combined with the low learning rate, freezing **underfits** instead (lr 1e-5 frozen: still improving at epoch 3, worst score 30.2%, WF 2023 only 19.8%). On the small WF 2023 period (3,190 training CVEs) no setting overfits within 3 epochs. The early-stopping + refit protocol caught every overfitting case (it chose 1–2 epochs exactly where the stopping-set loss turned up).
seeds: Over 2 seeds the chosen setting averages **34.6%** (seed 0: 36.8%, seed 1: **32.4%**), barely above the best rule (34.1%) and **4.9 points below the text MLP (39.5%)**. The 4.4-point gap between two seeds of the *same* setting is larger than the gap between the top three settings, so fine-tuning is also the least stable text model. **Decision 11b: the fine-tuned model does not beat the text MLP, so it does not enter the late fusion.** Likely reasons: only 25% of negatives, at most 3 epochs, and 22M parameters fit to a few hundred positives per period. The frozen encoder plus a small head generalises better with this little labelled data.
fusion: Applying Decision 11 exactly as written before these results: gradient boosting 47.4% vs late fusion (boosting + text MLP) 46.7%, within 2 points, so the better **worst period** decides → **late fusion is the final model (worst period 42.6% vs 39.7%)**, with gradient boosting as the simpler alternative. For transparency: a fusion with the fine-tuned model *would* score slightly higher (47.2%, worst 44.1%), but the difference is **one exploited CVE on val** (30 vs 29 of 68; identical counts on both walk-forward periods, 56/121 and 23/45, even though the scores differ, correlation 0.85–0.89). Since the pre-registered rule only lets the fine-tuned model in if it beats the text MLP on its own, we do not adopt it: switching now would be choosing on noise after seeing results.
ci: On val at K = 110 the fine-tuned model (2-seed ensemble) catches **25.0%** [15–36] of exploited CVEs: **−6.5 points vs the text MLP** (P(better) = 6%) and −2.8 vs the best rule (P = 33%). At K = 305 it does better (57.4% vs 50.0% for the text MLP), the same pattern as in 5b: text helps more once the obvious candidates are patched. Its recall-vs-K curve stays below the text MLP at small capacity, crosses it at ~200/month, and is the highest curve of all from ~600/month (≈ 90% recall), but those capacities are far above our K.
final: Fine-tuning the transformer **did not pay off**: 34.6% on the selection rule, below the frozen-encoder text MLP (39.5%) and only just above the best day-0 rule (34.1%), with large seed-to-seed swings and clear overfitting at the higher learning rate. **The final model under Decision 11 stays late fusion of gradient boosting and the text MLP** (selection 46.7%, best worst period 42.6%), with gradient boosting alone (47.4%) as the simpler alternative. Both will be scored once on test in Phase 6; only late fusion is the headline. Optional next rungs (domain-adaptive MLM pretraining) are unlikely to change this with our label count, and are not planned unless you want them.
